subject: Capacity corridor: smoothing reserve asks for upcoming closes
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2029 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity corridor: smoothing reserve asks for upcoming closes

Team —

We have three mid-to-large deals with close windows between 3–8 weeks that are starting to push hard on dedicated capacity requests. Rather than reacting deal-by-deal, I want to pilot a "capacity corridor" approach for the next 6 weeks to smooth requests and avoid overprovisioning. Attached: a working model (2029-06_capacity_corridor_model.xlsx).

Problem: deals fluctuate in probability and commit timing, which is causing spikes in reserved-slot asks and stress on burst credits. Proposal below is intentionally conservative.

Proposal (high level):
- Define a rolling 6-week corridor with a low and high capacity band (low = committed deals + 5% buffer; high = committed + soft-commit uplift + 25%).
- Smooth week-to-week deltas by limiting increases to a max of 15% of corridor baseline (to avoid sudden GPU procurement or reallocation).
- Mark deals as: firm commit, soft commit (sales confirms but no legal signature), and tentative.

Asks:
1) Jordan — can you feed the latest per-deal slot demand and close timing into the model by EOD Friday (6/14)?
2) Ben/Kimberly — validate whether the proposed 15% week-over-week uplift is operationally safe from an infra/burst perspective and list fallback variants (quantized model, lower sequence targets).
3) Laura — quick finance read: does this corridor improve cost predictability enough to justify converting some burst usage to reserved pricing?

If we can align quickly we'll present a single ask to Acme (and two others) that reduces frantic re-requests and gives Finance predictability. I booked a 30-min sync for Thu 6/15 10:30 PT — please accept if you can.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 09:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity corridor: smoothing reserve asks for upcoming closes

Vanessa — thanks for framing this. I loaded the current pipeline and ran a quick mapping to expected slot-days. Key outputs (summary, more in the attached sheet):

- ACME (ACME-2029-Q2-DED-57): close probability 70% in 4–6 weeks. Requested capacity: 200 A100-equivalent slot-days/week if full commit.
- Borealis Health: 40% probability, mid-July. Requested burst of ~80 slot-days/week.
- Nimbus Labs: 90% probability, signature expected in 3 weeks, 120 slot-days/week.

Current committed baseline across all deals = 220 slot-days/week. If we apply Vanessa's bands: low band = 231 (committed +5%), high band = committed + soft-commit uplift +25% = ~310. Week-over-week smoothing cap at 15% would allow growth in the early weeks without hitting 310 immediately.

Actionable items from me:
- I updated the model's 'sales certainty' column and flagged ACME as 'soft commit' pending SOW signature. Sheet shows per-week ramp if they move from soft to firm.
- I'll add per-deal preferred start date and a grace window for billing sync.

I think this gives Infra a more predictable ramp to plan for. Sharing model snapshot in thread.

Jordan
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations

Attachment: pipeline_slot_mapping_ACME_snapshot.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2029 11:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity corridor: smoothing reserve asks for upcoming closes

Appreciate the framing. Operational notes and constraints from Infra: 

- 15% w/w uplift is acceptable as a target but depends on distribution across regions and instance types. If ACME's 200 slots are all A100s in us-west, that's a tight ask for short notice.
- Fallbacks: we can serve initial traffic on 8-bit quantized variants and pre-warm KV caches to reduce end-to-end costs and slot-hours by ~18–25% while the reserved pool scales.
- Burst credits: we have ~1200 burst slot-days banked across accounts; recommend preserving at least 40% as contingency for multi-tenant outages.

Questions for Sales/Finance:
- What threshold turns a "soft commit" into a firm reserved slot order? (Is signature required or is 60% prepaid ok?)

I'll validate instance availability and post a week-by-week provisioning plan by Fri 6/14 EOD. If we need immediate capacity we should identify which deals can accept quantized variants.

Ben Carter
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity corridor: smoothing reserve asks for upcoming closes

Thanks — quick finance perspective:

- Reserved capacity economics: converting predictable usage from burst to reserved reduces unit cost ~28% but increases cash exposure. We need a 3-way tradeoff: probability * expected usage * duration to justify a reserved commit.
- For the corridor approach, recommend we mark: firm commit (legal signed) => reserve, soft commit (sales sign-off + procurement timeline <30 days) => reserved if Acme will provide 50–60% upfront payment, tentative => burst/quantized.
- For ACME specifically: if they can commit to 60% upfront at signature (Tim's note below), I'd be comfortable approving a phased reserved purchase: 40% of requested slots in week 1, 30% more at week 3, rest on signature finalization. That reduces our working capital risk.

One ask: can Sales produce a short input table with per-deal payment terms (upfront %, billing cadence) so Finance can model cash flow? I don't need full contract redlines — just the money cadence.

Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Thanks for the clarity. Acme is comfortable with the corridor concept. Quick answers from Procurement: 

- Procurement timeline: we can sign a finalized SOW within 10 business days once the scope and pricing are agreed.
- Payment terms: Acme can do 60% upfront on signature, remainder net 30. We attached SOW (ACME_SOW_v2.pdf) with specific slot/rate lines.
- Technical flex: Acme is open to a 2-week ramp where the first 30% of capacity may be on a lower-cost quantized variant while reserved fleet is provisioned.

Thanks everyone — decision and next steps summarized below. This thread will be our canonical record for the pilot.

Decisions (agreed):
- We will trial the 6-week capacity corridor for Q3 initial ramp. Low band = committed +5%; high band = committed + soft-commit uplift +25%.
- Week-over-week growth cap = 15% (Ben will validate per-region instance plans; Jordan to flag any single-deal concentration that violates this).
- Finance will accept staged reserved purchases for ACME if Acme provides 60% upfront at signature (Laura/Vanessa).
- Infra fallback: first 2 weeks can use quantized variants for up to 30% of traffic while reserved slots warm up (Ben).

Owners & deliverables:
- Jordan: finalize per-deal weekly slot schedule and mark 'firm/soft/tentative' by EOD Wed 6/19. (Deliverable: updated pipeline tab in the model)
- Ben: confirm instance availability and post the week-by-week provisioning plan + list of fallback variant types by Fri 6/21.
- Laura: run cash-flow model for phased reserved purchases and report impact to run-rate by Fri 6/21.
- Vanessa: consolidate external ask to Acme and request signature timeline; coordinate DocuSign link and finalize SOW pricing alignment.

Sync: keep Thu 6/15 10:30 PT on calendars for the initial sync — I'll re-use it for a quick roll-forward if needed.

If anyone objects to the plan above, speak now; otherwise I'll move to send the single external ask to Acme later today.
